questions.question: You want to put the important new information at the very end of the sentence, so you open the sentence with a 'What...' clause instead of leading with it. Which chunk fits best?

✓ Correct — "What surprised me most was..." is a Wh-clefts: highlighting via What chunk: used to push the key new information to the end of the sentence by opening with a What-clause.
Example: "What surprised me most was how quickly support tickets dropped after the fix."

- What it comes down to is...
- What struck me was...

✗ "From where I sit..." belongs to Personal viewpoint framing — used to preface a personal opinion so the listener knows it's a view, not a stated fact, not this context.
Similar chunks:
- The way I see it...
- If you want my view...
- The truth is...

✗ "On that basis" belongs to Formal transition connectors: consequence & purpose — used in a formal register to connect a consequence or next step to what was just said, not this context.
Similar chunks:

- Which brings me to...
- Which is exactly why...

✗ "If there's one takeaway..." belongs to Highlighting the key takeaway — used to flag the single most important fact after a longer explanation, not this context.
